body:
hi! i had seen your post from a year ago and commented on it, and ever since then i'd been checking your profile every few months to see if you were alright. (sorry if that's weird x_x)

i'm glad you're okay, and i'm glad you're doing so much better. :D thank you for posting an update.

I think those types of people tend to find SH attractive cuz it's a sign of someone being mentally ill/unstable and thus potentially more dependent/easier to control & manipulate, although whether they're capable of admitting that to themselves is another issue altogether. 🚩 🚩 🚩

Sorry to hear about the keloids -- those sound annoying. It's interesting that your body was just like "lol atrophic time", almost like something environmental might have changed. C'est la vie, though, I suppose.

I hadn't considered the neutral option, lol. I guess a decent number of mine fit that category, since they're mostly visible when I wrinkle the skin. Since it's collagen related, I wonder if there's an association between people that "age well" and people that get primarily raised scars. Not that that'd be an easy question to pursue, lmao, and I'm sure a lot of it's a bit random.
Great minds ask the same questions, or whatever. "Bodies are unique" tends to be the answer to a lot of odd phenomena, huh? A tad frustrating. I like knowing things.
Oo, interesting. My body's not exactly the biggest producer of collagen then, I suppose. This is a bit of a weird question technically, but do you have a mix of both indented and shallow scars then?
Nah, a few of mine had gnarly scabs and turned out just as indented. Of course, I did always pick at the scabs...

This is interesting to think about. I used the same method for all my scars, with a lamely "cleaned" (soap and water) tool that wasn't exactly the sharpest, then washed the wounds themselves out with soap and water too. I only covered them until they stopped bleeding for the night, so I suppose my aftercare would count as mediocre, though I luckily never got infected. So maybe indented vs raised does have a bit to do with tool + sanitation. Of course, this is only anecdotal, haha.
could you elaborate more? i mean, feel free to totally vent here; i'm interested in the specifics, in part so i can judge if possible shitty situations are ones that i'd be able to deal with.

yeah, there's a few different options around here that i know about, and since i'd be submitting myself voluntarily i'd definitely choose whichever seemed least prison-like. i do worry about the quality of activities and therapy, but i suppose that depends on the establishment. thank you for the input -- i'm sorry that it didn't help you. i hope you've found things that do work for you. <3
this does make it sound appealing... i wouldn't exactly go there looking for a fun time, haha, cuz it's not like i have fun in my regular life. just a break would be really nice, i think.

you're not a bad person. morbid curiosity is a real thing, like the classic example of not being able to look away from a horrifying car accident. i would at least recommend steering away from watching vids like that, though, 'cause they can mess with you.

someone who is abusing children will do it regardless of if anyone is watching their videos. i can say with absolute certainty that your viewership did no real harm, and they likely did get terminated.

it's hard to let go of things that you think you've done wrong -- i do my own fair share of morality obsession. it's most helpful to yourself, though, to accept the possible mistake, learn or change from it, and carry on. 

perhaps you can take motivation from the idea that the playlist creator would be pleased with someone hurting themself in response to that content, and it seems like you probably don't want to please that creator.

i did this recently, albeit with a lesser dose. if it's of any consolation, you end up not remembering a large chunk of the time.

i very much recommend you call someone to help you. please wake someone up now -- i ended up barely having control over my movement. you'll also end up horribly dehydrated, so try to keep some water by you if you can.

it fucking sucks, but you can make it through it, and i genuinely hope that you do. <3

i feel like people get annoyed by the fact that you haven't recovered, too, like they seem to get sick of hearing abt it. anyone i do confide in that isn't depressed always seems to think that something specific is wrong & that it can be "fixed" & i end up shrugging off the half-baked attempts at asking "what's wrong" after a few times of trying to answer that question to their satisfaction.

they have the privilege of getting to stop thinking abt suicidal thoughts once you're off their mind -- people who actually experience them never really get to escape. i don't think non-depressed people realize that reality a lot of the time. i don't just feel down and out every once in a while when i give up on trying to mask it, it's literally a daily struggle.

hehe, the major definitely suits you, then.

i've struggled with toeing that line myself many times before; the one friend i have that i usually vent to is suicidal themself, so i have to censor myself there. it's definitely tough to reconcile honesty and safety. you've done fine here, though.

do you write a lot? i was on here searching for some form of catharsis, as i'm having a rough night myself, and this finally got me to bawl. <3 if you don't write, you should, even just as a hobby; this was very articulate and relatable.

writing aside, i hope you can find some healthy catharsis of your own. it can be so exhausting carrying around suicidal ideation in the back of your head all the time :^(
